p: Sextus Pompeius Magnus Pius was the son of Pompey by his third wife, Mucia Tertia, with an elder brother, Gnaeus Pompeius, and a sister, Pompeia. When Julius Caesar crossed the Rubicon in 49 BCE, Gnaeus followed their father to the East while Sextus stayed in Rome in the care of his stepmother, Cornelia Metella. After the defeat at the Battle of Pharsalus in 48 BCE the two met Pompey on Lesbos and fled with him to Egypt, where Sextus watched his father killed by treachery on 29 September of that year.

He then joined the resistance to Caesar in the African provinces alongside Metellus Scipio, Cato the Younger and his brother. Caesar defeated the Pompeius brothers at the Battle of Munda in Hispania in 45 BCE. Gnaeus died soon afterwards in a last stand at Lauro; Sextus escaped and raised another army in Spain.

After Caesar's death Mark Antony moved that Sextus be recalled, paid 50 million Attic drachmas for his father's confiscated property and given command of the whole Roman navy. He accepted, but went no further than Massilia before returning to Sicily. When the Second Triumvirate began its proscriptions, many of the proscribed fled to him, and after the battles of Philippi in 42 BCE survivors of the party of Brutus and Cassius did the same. With the whole island as his base he built an army and a strong navy.

In 40 BCE his admiral, the freedman Menas, seized Sardinia from Octavian's governor Marcus Lurius. By the Pact of Misenum in 39 BCE the triumvirs recognised his control of Sicily and Sardinia in exchange for keeping the grain supply to Rome open and his pirates in check. The peace was short. Each side accused the other of breaking it, and Menas betrayed Sardinia to Octavian. Sextus defeated Octavian at sea off Messina in 37 BCE.

Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa spent a winter building and training a fleet near Lake Avernus. He fought Sextus at Mylae in August 36 BCE, Marcus Aemilius Lepidus and Titus Statilius Taurus invaded Sicily, and after Naulochus Sextus fled to Asia Minor. Captured in 35 BCE, he was put to death without trial at Miletus by Marcus Titius, whom he had once spared, either on Titius's own initiative or possibly on the orders of Antony or Plancus. Plutarch gives him a minor role in the fall of the Republic; Appian treats him as a central figure who might even have emerged as the final victor.

notes: The article says Sextus escaped 'to Sicily' after Munda and then raised an army in Spain; that reads oddly, so I wrote only that he escaped and raised an army in Spain.
The article's chronology has him defeat Octavian in August 36 BCE while the text has Agrippa fight him at Mylae that month; I gave only the text's wording.
The article writes 'stolen property'; I wrote 'confiscated', which may be more than it says: change back if wanted.
